chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of joking, for it draws out foolishness, begets enmity, and it is the minor insult.'

key_terms.السَّخِيمَةَ: Foolishness, silliness, or lack of seriousness

ai.seo_question: What are the negative consequences of joking according to Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns against excessive joking (al-mizah), identifying it as a gateway to foolishness (al-sakheemah) and latent enmity (al-dagheenah) that can escalate into conflict. He further characterizes it as 'the minor insult' (al-sabb al-asghar), suggesting that while it may seem harmless, it erodes dignity and social harmony, a concept deeply valued in Shia ethical teachings (adab). This advice underscores the importance of maintaining composure and sincerity in speech to preserve interpersonal relationships.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from IbnAl Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Beware of the joking for it would (cause) the grudges to flow, and would inherit the hatred, and it is the small insult’.
en.sarwar: 12. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘Beware of joking; it attracts hatred and hostility and it is a minor form of name-calling.’”
